ErrorBucket.description: One error code, and how much of the failure it accounts for.

class.description:
Whose failure it is.

`SERVER` is a 5xx, `CLIENT` a 4xx, `NETWORK` a timeout, reset or DNS failure — which is the distinction between a fault the operator can fix and one the caller can.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

count.description:
How many requests failed this way.

A 64-bit integer. Sent either quoted or bare; always returned quoted.

termId.description: Term id for the human explanation, e.g. `err.500`.

trend.description:
Which way the count is moving.

Which way a figure moved. Not whether that is good news — for availability up is better, for error rate it is worse.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

HistoryMapping.description: Where the nested daily series is, if the upstream offers one. Omit it and the dashboard rolls up its own buckets from successive polls instead — which is why a pull deployment need not supply history at all.

date.description: Path to the day, within a point. Required: a point that cannot be placed in time is dropped.

errorRate.description: Path to the day's error rate.

latencyP50.description: Path to the day's median latency.

path.description: Path to the array of daily points, relative to each record.

volume.description: Path to the day's request count.

availability.description: Percent, 0–100, over the day. Absent is not zero.

day.description:
UTC midnight of the day this bucket covers.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

latencyP50Ms.description: Median response time over the day, in milliseconds.

samples.description: How many raw readings were folded into this bucket. Zero for a bucket supplied whole by an upstream rather than rolled up locally.

volume.description:
Requests over the day.

A 64-bit integer. Sent either quoted or bare; always returned quoted.

Incident.description: One interruption, with the timeline of what was done about it.

closedAt.description:
When it ended. Absent while it is still open.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

events.description: What happened and when, oldest first.

noteTermId.description: Term id for the one-line summary shown to a reader.

openedAt.description:
When it began.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

severity.description:
Only `STATUS_MAJOR` and `STATUS_PARTIAL` are meaningful here.

The verdict. A fixed vocabulary, not a configurable one: the threshold rules are tied to these five outcomes, so a sixth would be a contract change. Config controls each one's label, glyph, colour and thresholds.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

at.description:
When the stage was reached.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

type.description: Free-form, so a deployment can model its own lifecycle. Displayed through the term id `inc.<type>`, which means adding a stage is a locale key rather than a contract change. Well-known values: `opened`, `acknowledged`, `mitigated`, `resolved`.

IngestError.description: One reason one record was dropped. A single record can produce several.

field.description: Which field, as a dotted JSON path — `metrics.availability`, `scope`.

message.description: What was wrong with it, in plain words.

serviceId.description: The `id` of the record concerned, empty if that was what was missing.

IngestRequest.description: One batch of observations. Send as JSON or as binary protobuf; the endpoint decides on `Content-Type` and defaults to JSON, so a collector that sets none at all still works.

mode.description:
Whether this payload adds to what the dashboard holds or replaces it. Omitted, it upserts.

How this payload relates to what the dashboard already holds. `INGEST_MODE_UNSPECIFIED` is treated as an upsert.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

services.description: The observations. An empty list is accepted and changes nothing in upsert mode; in replace mode it empties the dashboard.

sourceId.description: Free-form label for the collector, so several feeding one dashboard stay distinguishable in its logs.

IngestResponse.description: What was stored, and what was not. Always 200 when the body decoded: a malformed record in a batch of two hundred does not reject the other hundred and ninety-nine.

accepted.description: How many records were stored. Omitted when none were.

errors.description: Why each dropped record was dropped.

receivedAt.description:
The server's clock when it handled the request.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

rejected.description: How many records were dropped. Omitted when none were.

IngestService.description: One service as its operator observed it. Deliberately smaller than the record the read API returns: status, trends and rank movement are absent rather than ignored, because a deployment reports observations and the dashboard decides verdicts.

callsKey.description: For a requestor, the `key` of the issuer it calls. This is what builds the demand side: who pulls what, and how much of it.

categoryId.description: Must be one of the categories declared in the deployment's `domain.yaml`, e.g. `cat.identity`. An undeclared value rejects the record, because a category no filter offers is a service no reader can find.

descTermId.description: Term id for the one-line description, resolved like `nameTermId`.

errors.description: The error codes behind the error rate, as buckets. Like incidents, reachable only through push.

history.description: Sealed daily buckets, oldest first. Optional: supply them to backfill the charts immediately, or omit them and the dashboard rolls its own up from successive observations.

id.description: Stable identifier, and the key an upsert merges on. Required — a record without one is rejected and the rest of the batch is still stored.

incidents.description: Open and recent incidents, with their timeline. There is no way to express these through a pull mapping, so a deployment that wants them uses push.

key.description: Short slug. A requestor's `callsKey` names the issuer it calls by this, so an issuer other records point at needs one.

maintenance.description: Planned work in progress, which suppresses the outage verdict for its duration.

metrics.description: The current reading. What the status is derived from.

nameTermId.description: Term id resolved against the reader's locale, e.g. `svc.aadhaar.name`. A deployment that does not translate can send literal text: the resolver falls through to the raw string when no key matches.

observedAt.description:
When the upstream took this reading. Absent, the server stamps its own receipt time — which is a different claim, so send it if you know it.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

ownErrorShare.description: Percent, 0–100, of a requestor's errors that are its own rather than the publisher's — a 4xx it sent, not a 5xx it received. A requestor told only its error rate has a number it cannot act on.

providerId.description: Term id for the operating body, e.g. `prov.uidai`. Not validated against the taxonomy.

regionId.description: Must be one of the regions declared in `domain.yaml`, e.g. `reg.national`. Validated like `categoryId`.

roleId.description: Which side of the exchange this is: `issuer` for a service that publishes a document, `requestor` for an organisation that consumes one. Empty means the deployment's default role.

scope.description: Which view the service belongs to — the deployment's declared scopes, `national` or `state` as shipped. Validated; an undeclared value rejects the record.

sectorId.description: For a requestor, the sector running the use case, e.g. `sec.banking`. Empty for an issuer, which consumes nothing.

subscriptionType.description: How a requestor is subscribed to the API it calls, e.g. `document` or `service`.

generatedAt.description:
When this snapshot was assembled.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

services.description: One record per service, in the order the source supplied them.

Maintenance.description: Planned work, which suppresses the outage verdict while it is in progress.

active.description: Whether work is in progress now.

reasonTermId.description: Term id for the reason shown to a reader, e.g. `maint.scheduled`.

until.description:
When it is expected to end.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

MappingSpec.description: The same structure `pull.endpoints[].` takes in `config/sources.yaml`, key for key — so a block that works here can be pasted straight into the file, and a block from the file can be pasted here to find out what it does.

itemsPath.description: Path to the array of records, e.g. `$.data.services[*]`. Empty means the document is itself the array. The syntax is deliberately small: `$.a.b`, `$.items[0]`, `$.items[*]` and combinations. No filters, no recursive descent, no expressions.

map.description: Dashboard field name to a path into each record. `id` must be mapped, because without it services cannot be told apart.

transform.description: Field name to the chain applied after reading it. Chains run in order, and an absent value skips every step except `default`.

availability.description: Percent, 0–100 — `99.92`, not `0.9992`. **Absent is not zero.** A missing reading yields `STATUS_UNKNOWN`; a zero says the service is wholly down. A value between 0 and 1 is accepted, because a genuine 0.9% availability has to stay reportable, but it is logged as a probable ratio-for-percent mistake.

staleSeconds.description:
How old the reading is. Past the deployment's `staleSecondsAbove` threshold the status becomes `STATUS_UNKNOWN`, because a stale reading is not evidence that anything is working.

A 64-bit integer. Sent either quoted or bare; always returned quoted.

volume.description: Request counts over the reporting window.

PullPreviewRequest.description: An upstream's document, and the mapping under consideration. Nothing is fetched: the document travels in the body, so this endpoint cannot be used to make the dashboard issue requests from inside its own network.

document.description: The JSON your upstream would serve, verbatim.

PullPreviewResponse.description: What the dashboard would make of it — including the status it would derive, which is the part a mapping cannot be checked against by eye.

services.description: One per record the mapping read, evaluated exactly as a poll would evaluate it.

skipped.description: Records the mapping could not read. A poller logs these and carries on; here they are the answer.

index.description: Position in the source array, from zero.

reason.description: Why it could not be read.

Service.description: One service as the dashboard holds it: what was reported, and what it concluded.

callsKey.description: For a requestor, the `key` of the issuer it calls.

descTermId.description: Term id for the one-line description.

errors.description: The error codes behind the error rate.

key.description: Short slug. A requestor's `callsKey` matches on this.

nameTermId.description: Term id for the display name.

observedAt.description:
When the reading was taken.

RFC 3339, in UTC.

ownErrorShare.description: Percent of a requestor's errors that are its own.

providerId.description: Term id for the operating body.

rankMovement.description: **Derived, output only.** Places moved since the previous snapshot.

scope.description: Which view the service belongs to.

sectorId.description: For a requestor, the sector running the use case.

status.description:
**Derived, output only.** Recomputed on every snapshot from `metrics` against the thresholds the deployment publishes, so the rule shown on screen is provably the rule that was applied. Sending one has no effect; the ingest message has no field for it.

The verdict. A fixed vocabulary, not a configurable one: the threshold rules are tied to these five outcomes, so a sixth would be a contract change. Config controls each one's label, glyph, colour and thresholds.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

subscriptionType.description: How a requestor is subscribed to the API it calls.

TransformStep.description: One step of a transform chain.

by.description: For `multiply`, `divide` and `round`. Non-zero for the first two.

fn.description: Which transform. A value that cannot be coerced to the type the transform needs passes through untouched rather than becoming zero.

table.description: For `enumMap`: the lookup. An unmapped value passes through unchanged, so a table that misses a case leaves the original rather than emptying the field.

value.description: For `default` and `trimPrefix`. Note that `default` fires only for a field that has a `map` entry: an unmapped field is absent, not defaulted.

Trend.description: **Derived, output only.** How a metric has moved over the trend window.

delta.description: The change, in the metric's own units.

direction.description:
Which way it moved. Better or worse depends on the metric.

Which way a figure moved. Not whether that is good news — for availability up is better, for error rate it is worse.

Sent as the name or as the number; always returned as the name.

periodDays.description: How many days the comparison covers.

Volume.description: Request counts over the reporting window.

success.description:
Requests that succeeded. More successes than requests rejects the record.

A 64-bit integer. Sent either quoted or bare; always returned quoted.

total.description:
Requests received.

A 64-bit integer. Sent either quoted or bare; always returned quoted.

ingestToken.description: The value of the environment variable named by `push.tokenEnvVar` in `config/sources.yaml`, shipped as `DPI_INGEST_TOKEN`. Never a value from a configuration file: a token in a config file ends up in a git history.

info.description:
Two ways to get data in, and they are alternatives rather than layers.

**Push** — your collector calls `POST /api/v1/ingest` whenever it has something to say. It is the richer of the two: incidents and error buckets can only arrive this way, and every record is validated against the deployment's own taxonomy, so a category nothing declares is rejected rather than quietly becoming unreachable.

**Pull** — the dashboard polls an endpoint you already have, on a timer, and maps its shape onto its own with a declarative mapping in `config/sources.yaml`. Nothing to build and nothing to schedule, but it can carry only what a mapping can express. `POST /api/v1/pull/preview` exists so that mapping can be worked out interactively rather than by editing a file and restarting.

Exactly one of the two is active, chosen by `driver:` in `config/sources.yaml`, so an operation this deployment does not register says so in its own description.

**What the dashboard decides for itself.** Status is never reported, only derived: a collector sends observations and the dashboard evaluates them against the thresholds it publishes. `status`, `trends` and `rankMovement` are absent from the ingest message rather than ignored, so the contract states it plainly.
info.summary: Feed a dashboard, read back what it holds, and try a pull mapping before committing to one.
info.title: White-label DPI dashboard

get.description: Every reader selection rides in the query string, so a shared link reproduces exactly what the sender was looking at. Unrecognised values fall back to the deployment's defaults rather than erroring: a hand-edited URL or a bookmark that outlived a config change should produce a sensible page, not an empty one.

Deliberately **not** the dashboard's own schema: ratios rather than percentages, `IDENTITY` rather than `cat.identity`, and field names nothing here chose. It exists so the shipped pull mapping has something real to poll, which makes switching to your own service one URL change against a path already proven to work.

Served when the dashboard holds its own data — `driver: seed` or `driver: push`. Under `driver: pull` it is absent, so a deployment cannot re-publish a copy of what it polls.
get.summary: The same data in a foreign shape

get.description: This reference, rendered, with every request editable and sendable against the running deployment. Served everywhere, so a deployment always carries its own documentation.
The committed document, overlaid with what is true of this particular deployment: the server URL it is being served from, and a note on any operation the configured driver does not register.

post.description:
Send what you have observed. Everything else the dashboard shows is derived from it.

Partial acceptance is deliberate: a malformed record in a batch of two hundred does not reject the other hundred and ninety-nine. The response is `200` whenever the body decoded, and says which records were dropped and why — so a collector checks `rejected`, not the status code.

The complete worked payload is committed at `examples/push/payload.json`; the example below is the first two records of it.

minimal.description: One service, one reading. Everything else the dashboard shows — the status, the trend, the rank — is worked out from this.

seeded.description: The first two records of `examples/push/payload.json`, history and error buckets trimmed. The complete file is what `make demo-push` sends.

partial.description: The status is still 200. A collector checks `rejected`, not the status code — which is what lets one bad record out of two hundred stay one bad record.
partial.summary: One record dropped, the rest stored

200.description: Decoded. Read `accepted` and `rejected` to find out what happened to it.

400.description: The body could not be decoded: empty, over the size limit, not valid JSON or protobuf, or carrying a field the contract does not declare.

401.description: No bearer token, or the wrong one. The response says nothing about which, because telling an unauthenticated caller why their token was rejected helps them guess at a valid one.

post.description:
Pull is a contract the dashboard consumes rather than an endpoint it serves, so a mapping normally cannot be tried at all: you edit `sources.yaml`, restart, and look at the board. This runs the same three steps a poll runs — compile the mapping, apply it to the document, evaluate the result — with the fetch left out.

Leaving the fetch out is deliberate. An endpoint that accepted a URL and retrieved it would let anyone use the dashboard to make requests from inside its own network, so the document travels in the body.

The response carries the **derived** status, which is what makes it worth running: a mapping can read every field it was asked to and still produce a board of unknowns, because availability arrived as a ratio where a percentage was expected.

Registered whatever the configured driver — it touches no state.

minimal.description: `id` is the only field a mapping must have — without it, records cannot be told apart. Everything unmapped is absent rather than zero.

shipped.description: One record of `examples/upstream/services.json` with the mapping from `config/sources.yaml`. Note what the transforms are for: the upstream reports availability as a ratio and category as `IDENTITY`, and neither would mean anything to the dashboard untranslated.

200.description: What the dashboard would make of the document.

400.description: The body could not be read, or the mapping would not compile. The message names the field and lists what was expected — an unknown field name, a path that does not parse, a transform that needs an operand it was not given, or `id` left unmapped.

post.summary: Try a pull mapping without deploying it

get.description:
The same records the pages are drawn from, with the derived fields included — `status`, `trends` and `rankMovement`, none of which any feed can set.

Unauthenticated, because it returns exactly what the public HTML already shows: gating the machine-readable form of a page anyone can load would be theatre rather than access control.
Built at startup from `config/theme.yaml`, never a file on disk. Served immutable with a fingerprint for an ETag, so a restyled deployment produces a different URL rather than a stale cache.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag the request carried.

get.description: The stylesheet, the script, htmx, the fonts and the API console's renderer, all compiled into the binary. Served immutable for a year, which is safe because every link carries a `?v=` fingerprint over the whole embedded tree.
The whole panel, for opening one.
